Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We saw robust growth in our midstream transportation volumes and key infrastructure projects advancing on schedule. Our refining operations hit high utilization rates with impressive crack spreads, while exploration and drilling yielded standout well results that de-risked significant acreage. We're maintaining disciplined capital spending focused on high-return opportunities. Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.2 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow and returned $500 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $8 billion in debt and $2.5 billion in cash.

Good morning, everyone. Let me now turn to our midstream segment, which continues to deliver resilient, fee-based cash flows and remains a cornerstone of our integrated model here at Apex Energy Corp. In the third quarter, midstream generated $450 million in adjusted EBITDA, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, representing 32% of our total segment EBITDA. This performance underscores the defensive nature of our largely take-or-pay contracts—over 85% of our midstream revenues are fixed or minimum volume commitment-backed, insulating us from commodity volatility even as WTI averaged $78 per barrel and Henry Hub gas held steady around $2.85 per MMBtu.

On transportation volumes, we saw robust execution amid sustained upstream production growth, particularly out of the Permian Basin. Total throughput across our system reached 1.85 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, a 12% increase year-over-year and beating our guidance midpoint by 3%. Breaking it down by commodity, crude oil volumes averaged 1.2 million barrels per day, up 15% year-over-year, driven by Permian takeaway capacity additions and our strategic positioning as a key egress provider. Utilization on our flagship Permian Express Pipeline system hit 92%, with average tariff realizations of $1.85 per barrel—up 4% from last year due to escalators tied to PPI and higher contracted rates on recent expansions. Notably, our Longhorn Pipeline extension, which came online in Q2, contributed an incremental 150,000 barrels per day, fully ramped to 95% utilization within 45 days.

Natural gas and NGLs totaled 3.7 billion cubic feet per day equivalent, up 8% year-over-year. Gas transportation on our Apex Gateway network averaged 2.5 billion cubic feet per day, benefiting from Marcellus dry gas production surges and growing LNG export demand. We transported 450,000 barrels per day of NGLs, with fractionation utilization at our Mont Belvieu facility at 88%, capturing $0.42 per gallon in fractionation spreads amid strong ethane demand from Gulf Coast crackers like ExxonMobil's Baytown expansion.

Regionally, the Permian Basin accounted for 65% of volumes, up from 58% last year, fueled by DCP Midstream and Occidental's drilling cadence—Permian rig counts remain elevated at 310 per Baker Hughes data. In the Bakken, volumes grew 10% to 180,000 barrels per day on our Dakota Link system, despite some weather-related curtailments in September. Appalachia contributed 20% of gas volumes, with our Mountain Valley Pipeline joint venture now fully in-service since late Q2, unlocking 2 billion cubic feet per day takeaway to Northeast markets and LNG feedgas at Cove Point.

Key trends include a shift toward longer-haul crude movements—average haul length up 7% to 450 miles—boosting revenue per barrel, and increasing NGL purity product specs meeting producer needs for Mont Belvieu pricing indices. We also navigated rail competition effectively; our pipe-to-rail flexibility at origin points kept volumes sticky, with only 2% displacement versus 2023 levels.

Turning to infrastructure development, we're executing a disciplined $1.2 billion capex program for 2024, focused on high-return, accretive projects with IRRs north of 12%. Year-to-date spend is $850 million, on track, yielding 650,000 boe/d of new capacity by year-end. Our marquee project, the Apex Permian Connector, a 42-inch, 200-mile greenfield pipeline from the Waha Hub to the Gulf Coast, is 85% mechanically complete. This $950 million venture, 50% owned by us, will add 800,000 barrels per day of crude capacity in Q4 2025, backed by 10-year take-or-pay contracts from EOG Resources and Pioneer at 90% MVC utilization. Engineering highlights include SCADA-integrated leak detection exceeding PHMSA standards and integration with our fiber-optic DAS for real-time monitoring, reducing O&M costs by 15%.

On the gas side, we're advancing the Gulf LNG Link expansion, a $400 million brownfield upgrade adding 1.2 billion cubic feet per day to feed Cheniere's Corpus Christi Stage 3 trains. Front-end engineering is complete, with FID expected Q1 2025 and in-service H2 2026. This positions us for the LNG export boom—U.S. feedgas demand projected to hit 14 billion cubic feet per day by 2027 per EIA—while incorporating CCUS tie-ins for 2 million tonnes per annum CO2 capture, aligning with our net-zero ambitions.

We've also progressed NGL infrastructure, debottlenecking our Hobbs fractionator by 25,000 barrels per day for $75 million, now at full capacity, and acquiring a 20% stake in a Bakken rail-to-pipe facility from a competitor for $150 million, enhancing hybrid logistics. Strategically, these investments de-risk our portfolio: 70% of new capacity is contracted pre-FID, with average contract life of 12 years and creditworthy anchors like Chevron and Devon. We're prioritizing Permian adjacency to capture 20%+ basin production growth forecasts from Enverus, while diversifying into Appalachia LNG to hedge basin-specific risks like Waha pricing discounts, which narrowed to -$0.15 per Btu in Q3.

Looking ahead, Q4 volumes guidance is 1.9-2.0 million boe/d, with midstream EBITDA of $460-480 million. Full-year capex holds at $1.2 billion, funding 10% volume growth in 2025. Risks include regulatory delays on FERC approvals—we've engaged proactively on NEPA reforms—and potential producer M&A consolidation, but our producer-agnostic model and dropdown potential from upstream partners mitigate this. In summary, midstream's volume momentum and infrastructure pipeline solidify our position as a top-tier midstream player, generating predictable FCF to support our 4.5% dividend yield and $2 billion buyback authorization.

Before I hand off, a quick note on our broader capital expenditure guidance for 2025 and our multi-year outlook through 2027, which underscores our relentless focus on capital discipline, high-return inventory, and value-accretive growth in this dynamic macro environment. With Brent averaging around $78 per barrel in Q3 and WTI at $74, our returns framework remains anchored to half-cycle breakevens below $45 WTI equivalent, ensuring robust free cash flow generation even in a lower-for-longer commodity price scenario.

For full-year 2025, we're guiding total capital expenditures to $4.8 billion, a modest 8% increase from our $4.45 billion spend in 2024. This reflects our commitment to returns over volume, with approximately 70% or $3.4 billion allocated to high-impact upstream drilling and completions, 20% or $950 million to base maintenance and infrastructure, and the balance of 10% or $450 million to strategic growth initiatives, including bolt-on M&A and low-carbon technologies. We're funding this entirely from operating cash flow, maintaining our net debt to EBITDA target below 1.0x and returning 50-60% of free cash flow to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

Breaking it down by key regions and programs, where we're prioritizing Tier 1 acreage with internal rates of return exceeding 25% at $65 WTI and sub-18 month paybacks. Permian Basin takes 65% of D&C spend at $2.2 billion: this remains our cash flow engine, accounting for over 60% of our 2025 production growth. We're planning 320 operated wells across our 250,000 net acre position in the Delaware and Midland basins, emphasizing cube-style developments with 12,000-15,000 foot laterals and 3,000 pounds per foot proppant intensity. Recent Delaware results mirror top-quartile peers like ExxonMobil and Occidental, with average 30-day IPs of 2,200 boe/d and breakevens at $38 WTI. We're deploying four new super-spec walking rigs from Patterson-UTI, incorporating our proprietary AI-driven geosteering platform, which has reduced drilling times by 15% and NPT by 20% year-over-year. Expect 2025 Permian volumes to ramp 12% to 180,000 boe/d, driving incremental NPV10 of over $1.2 billion at strip prices.

Eagle Ford and Bakken get 20% of D&C at $680 million: here, we're high-grading to oil-rich windows, targeting 85 wells with extended laterals and optimized frac designs. Eagle Ford Sligo hybrid completions are yielding 1,400 boe/d IPs at $42 breakevens, while Bakken Three Forks drilling mirrors Hess's strong analogs. This disciplined program supports 8% volume growth to 45,000 boe/d, with IRRs north of 30%.

Gulf of Mexico deepwater is 10% of D&C at $340 million: advancing our Winterfell tie-back and a new subsea development at our Avalanche prospect, we're partnering with Shell on high-pressure/high-temperature reservoirs. These projects leverage existing infrastructure for FIDs in H2 2025, with expected first oil in 2027 at 15,000 boe/d gross. Returns here are exceptional—35% IRR at $60 Brent—thanks to our salt weld imaging tech and alliances with TechnipFMC for all-electric subsea systems, cutting opex by 25%.

International and emerging plays are 5% of total capex at $240 million: offshore Guyana via our 15% stake in Block Stabroek, Exxon-led, sees $100 million in carry spend, with Liza Phase 3 ramping toward 220,000 bbl/d by 2026. In Brazil's pre-salt Santos Basin, we're progressing our Buzios appraisal with Petrobras, targeting FID in 2026. These are long-dated but transformative, with 40%+ IRRs.

On the tech and sustainability front, 15% of our capex or $720 million is earmarked for efficiency and energy transition plays. This includes $250 million for CO2 flood EOR pilots in the Permian, akin to Occidental's CDI initiatives, aiming to unlock 20% incremental recovery while sequestering 2 million tonnes CO2 annually for 45Q credits. We're also rolling out digital twin reservoir modeling with SLB's Delfi platform across 80% of our portfolio, boosting EURs by 10-15%. And in CCUS, our $150 million Polaris Hub in the Gulf Coast positions us for DOE grants, targeting 5 million tonnes per annum capture by 2030.

Looking multi-year, we see 2026-2027 capex flat to up 5% annually at $5.0-$5.2 billion, sustaining 5-7% organic production growth to 450,000 boe/d by 2027, with all-in returns averaging 28% IRR. This assumes OPEC+ discipline holds and no major service cost inflation, but our flexible rig contracts and supply chain hedging mitigate upside risks. Compared to peers, our inventory life exceeds Chevron's 15+ years of Tier 1 locations, and we're accretive on a DD&A per boe basis. In summary, this capex plan is returns-first, delivering $2.5+ billion in levered free cash flow at $70 WTI while de-risking our path to net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2050.

I will now turn the call over to Elena Vasquez for an operational update.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Blackhawk 12H-15H pad online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Good morning, everyone. Let me now turn to our refining segment, which delivered another strong quarter amid a volatile but favorable macro environment. As you know, our refining portfolio spans six world-scale facilities with a Nelson Complexity Index averaging 11.2, giving us a competitive edge in capturing value from heavy sour crudes like Western Canadian Select and Opportunity crude, while optimizing yields on lighter benchmarks such as WTI and Brent. Total nameplate capacity stands at 1.8 million barrels per day, with a strategic focus on high-octane gasoline, ultra-low sulfur diesel, and emerging renewable diesel pathways.

Starting with throughput, we averaged 1.250 million barrels per day in the third quarter, up 6% from 1.180 million bpd in Q3 last year and flat sequentially. This reflects a robust utilization rate of 92%, well above our long-term target of 88-90% and in line with peers like Valero and Marathon Petroleum. Key drivers included strong seasonal distillate demand in the US Midwest and Gulf Coast, where our Lima and Mandan refineries pushed throughput to 105% and 98% of capacity, respectively, processing a slate heavy in discounted Permian and Bakken intermediates.

Regionally, Gulf Coast assets—our El Paso and St. Charles complexes—averaged 850,000 bpd, benefiting from robust exports to Latin America and Europe, where product cracks remained elevated. We navigated a minor weather disruption from Hurricane Idalia, which shaved just 2 days of throughput at St. Charles, far less impactful than the 10-15% hits seen at competitor facilities in 2022's Ian aftermath. In Canada, our Edmonton refinery hit record throughput of 140,000 bpd on dilbit runs, leveraging TC Energy's expanded mainline capacity. Internationally, our 50% stake in the Dublin refinery maintained steady 120,000 bpd amid softer European demand, offset by premium jet cracks from summer travel rebound.

Turning to margins, we realized $22.40 per barrel in Q3, a 28% increase from $17.50 in the prior-year quarter and up 5% sequentially—our strongest since Q4 2022. This was fueled by robust crack spreads: the 3-2-1 Midwest crack averaged $22.50 per bbl, Gulf Coast $24.80, and our system-wide blended $23.10, per OPIS data. Diesel cracks were the star, averaging $35 per bbl on the NYMEX ULSD-WTI spread, driven by global supply tightness from Russian sanctions and Red Sea disruptions, which we've seen tighten ultra-low sulfur diesel differentials by 15-20% year-over-year.

Gasoline cracks held firm at $18 per bbl, Gulf Coast RBOB, supported by summer driving season and E10 blending economics, though softening slightly into shoulder months. Our margin outperformance versus the benchmark—$1.30 per bbl capture premium—stemmed from slate optimization: we shifted 15% more volume to high-value distillates, 58% yield versus 55% last year, boosted by hydrocracker utilization at 98%. Renewable volumes added $2.50 per bbl uplift via D4 RINs trading at $1.80 per gallon and California LCFS credits. Hedging contributed modestly, with 40% of Q4 cracks protected at $20 per bbl floors. Comparatively, this edges peers; Phillips 66 captured $21.80, while PBF lagged at $19.50 on heavier turnaround schedules.

On operational efficiency, we continue to drive best-in-class metrics. Total refining opex fell 8% year-over-year to $4.20 per barrel, below our $4.50 guidance and 5% better than the peer average per Solomon Associates benchmarking. Energy intensity improved 4% to 85,000 BTU per bbl equivalent, thanks to our digital twin initiatives at Mandan and El Paso, which use AI-driven predictive analytics to optimize furnace firing and heat exchanger performance—yielding $15 million in annualized savings.

Variable costs per throughput barrel dropped to $2.80 from $3.10 last year, driven by lower natural gas prices, $2.50 per MMBtu Henry Hub, and procurement discipline on hydrogen and caustic. Maintenance spend totaled $120 million, focused on a phased turnaround at St. Charles' coker and alkylation units, completing 20% ahead of schedule with zero LTIs. Post-turnaround, distillate yields are up 2 points, and we're targeting 95%+ hydrocracker runs in Q4. Sustainability efforts advanced: our renewable diesel train at Lima now processes 10,000 bpd of soybean oil and used cooking oil, hitting 85% nameplate with $45 per bbl margins—positioning us ahead of CVR and Delek in the pre-treated feedstock race.

Strategically, we're leaning into resilience and growth. We've idled 50,000 bpd of low-complexity hydroskimming capacity at a Midwest asset to prioritize high-return runs, unlocking $30 million in EBITDA. Looking ahead, Q4 throughput guidance is 1.220-1.280 million bpd at 90-94% utilization, with margins of $18-22 per bbl assuming stable geopolitics. Capex remains $400 million for 2024, funding pretreaters for heavier Canadian crudes and Phase 2 renewables expansion to 25,000 bpd by 2025—targeting 10% of throughput from sustainable fuels amid IRA incentives.

Demand tailwinds persist: US distillate stocks are 15 million barrels below 5-year averages per EIA, and global refinery runs lag 2% year-over-year due to maintenance waves in Asia. Risks include potential Canadian wildfires or OPEC+ cuts pressuring crude discounts, but our slate flexibility and 60-day inventory buffer mitigate this. In summary, refining generated $650 million in EBITDA—up 35% year-over-year—proving the durability of our integrated model.

Finally, on exploration and drilling activity updates, our team has executed flawlessly amid a supportive macro environment, with WTI holding steady around $82 per barrel and Brent at $86, bolstered by ongoing OPEC+ production cuts and resilient global demand. We've maintained capital discipline while advancing our high-return inventory. In Q3, we brought online 28 gross operated wells across our core acreage, achieving a 98% success rate—our highest quarterly mark in three years. This compares favorably to peers like Pioneer and EOG, who reported 95-96% in their recent prints. Our drilling and completion efficiency continues to improve, with average cycle times down 12% year-over-year to 95 days from spud to first oil, driven by pad drilling and optimized rig moves. Total D&C capital deployed was $450 million, in line with our 50/50 split between Permian and Eagle Ford, representing 28% of our full-year capex budget.

Drilling down into key well results by region, starting with the Permian Basin, which accounts for 65% of our D&C activity and 70% of our 2024 drilling inventory. We spudded 18 wells in the Midland Basin, targeting the Lower Spraberry and Wolfcamp A/B benches. Standout performers include the Blackhawk 12H-15H pad in Upton County, where four extended-lateral wells—averaging 12,500-foot laterals—posted initial production rates averaging 1,450 boe/d, with 82% oil cut. That's 28% above our internal type curve and right in line with top-quartile results from Occidental and Diamondback in similar intervals. Estimated ultimate recovery per well is now modeled at 1.8 million boe, up from our pre-drill estimate of 1.5 million, thanks to enhanced completions: we're running 2,500 pounds of proppant per foot with slickwater-dominant fluids and dissolvable diverters, which boosted stage-level productivity by 15%.

We've also pushed the envelope on child-well performance. The infill wells on this pad saw only a 7% productivity dip versus our parent wells from 2022—far better than the 20-25% observed industry-wide. This is attributable to our proprietary microseismic mapping and AI-optimized frac designs, in collaboration with Halliburton, which minimize parent-child interference. Net to our 72% working interest, these wells add 4,200 boe/d to production, with breakevens at $42 WTI—well below current strips.

In the Delaware Basin, our Q3 tests in the Second Bone Spring encountered unexpectedly rich liquid yields, with IP30s of 1,100 boe/d, 75% liquids. While smaller scale, these de-risk 15,000 net acres for future development, and we're incorporating learnings into our Q4 program.

Shifting to Eagle Ford, our program delivered another strong quarter with 10 wells online, focused on the oil window in Karnes and DeWitt counties. The Mustang 5H-8H pad—three-mile laterals targeting the Lower Eagle Ford Shale—averaged 1,200 boe/d IP30, 68% oil, 25% NGLs, exceeding our type curve by 22%. Proppant intensity here hit 2,200 lbs/ft, with engineered diverter cycles every three stages, resulting in 35% higher propped fracture surface area per our fiber-optic diagnostics.

These results underscore our shift toward oil-rich cores; gas-heavy Karnes acreage is now less than 10% of our queue. Compared to peers like EOG, our Eagle Ford F&D costs remain in the low $7/boe decile, supporting 60%+ IRRs at $80 WTI. We've also reduced fresh water usage by 40% via brackish recycling partnerships with Solaris, aligning with our ESG targets.

On the frontier side, we announced a significant discovery offshore in the Gulf of Mexico. Our Highlander #1 well in Green Canyon Block 298—drilled to 22,000 feet with Valaris' DS-10 rig—flowed 8,200 boe/d on test, 85% liquids, from Miocene sands, with 400 feet of net pay. Gross recoverable resources are estimated at 150-250 million boe, contingent on appraisal. This builds on our 2023 Keathley Canyon success and positions us for partnerships similar to Chevron's Anchor project. We're budgeting $120 million for two appraisal sidetracks in Q4.

Internationally, our Namibia PEL 82 farm-in with Galp Energia yielded promising 2D seismic reprocessing. The Mopane-1X well spud is on track for Q1 2025, targeting Venus-like fan systems with 500 million boe potential.

Underpinning these results are several initiatives. First, our in-house seismic AI platform, powered by SLB's Delfi, has cut interpretation time by 60% and improved sweet-spot accuracy to 92%. Second, we're standardizing on electric frack fleets from ProFrac, reducing emissions by 45% and flaring to under 1%, ahead of our 2025 net-zero D&C goal. Third, longer laterals, up 20% year-over-year to 11,000 feet average, and simultaneous operations on pads have driven D&C costs down 8% to $850 per lateral foot in Permian—competitive with the lowest-cost operators.

Rig count trends support our momentum: Permian utilization is at 310 rigs, up 5% quarter-over-quarter, but service inflation is moderating at 2-3% versus 10% last year. We're locked in 80% of our 2024 services at favorable rates.

Looking ahead, we'll spud 120 gross operated wells in 2024, flat year-over-year, with 70% in Permian, 25% Eagle Ford, and 5% Gulf/exploration. Q4 capex ramps to $500 million, targeting 32 wells online. Full-year D&C spend is $1.8 billion, fully funded from cash flow at current prices. Strategically, we're prioritizing inventory quality over quantity: 4.2 years of Tier 1 locations, IRR over 50% at $60 WTI, with 60% developed by 2027. M&A remains opportunistic—we closed a 5,000-acre bolt-on in Midland for $180 million in Q3, adding 20 locations at $25,000 per acre. Divestitures of non-core gas assets are progressing, targeting $300 million proceeds to high-grade the portfolio.

Risks include takeaway constraints in Permian—Waha averaged -15% in Q3—but our 90% hedged oil volumes and WES midstream stake mitigate this. We're also advancing CCUS pilots in Eagle Ford, positioning for IRA tax credits. In summary, our exploration and drilling engine is firing on all cylinders, delivering peer-leading returns and optionality. This supports our raised FY24 production guidance to 185-195 thousand boe/d, up 8% at midpoint, and $2.2-2.4 billion free cash flow.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Chen: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the transportation volumes in the midstream segment, particularly Permian contributions?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, David. As Michael outlined, Permian volumes drove 65% of our throughput, up from 58% last year, thanks to steady rig activity and new capacity like the Longhorn extension. We're seeing strong utilization and tariff growth, positioning us well for Q4 guidance of 1.9 to 2.0 million boe per day.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: Good morning. What are your expectations for capital expenditure allocation in the Permian next year?

Michael Rivera: Thanks, Lisa. Permian gets the lion's share at $2.2 billion, or 65% of D&C, funding 320 wells with cube developments and AI geosteering for 12% volume growth. Returns stay above 25% IRR at $65 WTI, fully cash flow funded.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Good morning. Could you please provide more color on the refining margins outlook and the Eagle Ford drilling results?

Elena Vasquez: Morning, Robert. Margins guidance for Q4 is $18 to $22 per barrel, supported by tight distillate markets and our slate shifts, with renewables adding uplift. On Eagle Ford, the Mustang pad exceeded type curves by 22% at 1,200 boe/d IP30, with optimized fracs driving high IRRs and lower water use.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
